prior_narrative.tldr: This thread groups ten items that share overlapping title words, not one developing story. It opened Aug 24-25 with three general-purpose anomaly-detection papers, then Aug 27-Sep 10 added a clinical-assistant comparison, two hallucination-detection papers, an agent-swarm benchmark, an HVAC deployment review, and a vendor business-model roundup -- none connected beyond the words 'detection' or 'large language models.'
prior_narrative.whats_new: The newest addition isn't a new event -- it's three unrelated anomaly-detection papers (relational databases, industrial control systems, streaming video) from Aug 24-25 that joined this page purely because they share the word 'detection' with the hallucination-detection paper already here, and none of the three mention LLMs at all.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: None of these ten items report on the same product, model, or event -- treat this page as a keyword collision, not a thread whose story to follow.

beats.headline: Three unrelated anomaly-detection papers join the thread on a shared word, not a shared subject
beats.summary: Relational-database, industrial-control-system, and streaming-video anomaly detection -- none mention large language models.

beats.headline: Three assistants, one clinical task: ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek compared on cardiac imaging patient education
Single-pass hallucination detector reads internal activations instead of sampling outputs
SwarmBench tests LLMs as orchestrators of dynamically-formed agent swarms
A second hallucination detector targets medical chatbot answers via multi-perspective adjudication
Critical review surveys LLM deployment readiness for HVAC building-energy operations
Weekend roundup contrasts Zhipu and MiniMax as two distinct LLM business models
Domain-specific hallucination detector pairs fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification with Monte Carlo sampling

open_questions: Does PoP's detection rate hold against sampling-based baselines such as semantic entropy, and at what accuracy cost?
Do PoP's inter-layer activation features transfer across model families, or must a detector be trained per model?
Does activation-level detection need weights access, ruling it out for API-only deployments?
Does SwarmBench report results for today's popular agent frameworks, or only for research prototypes?
Does the DeBERTa-v3 domain-specific hallucination detector generalize across domains, or need per-domain fine-tuning?
Do the three anomaly-detection papers (RAD, ICS robustness, streaming video) touch LLM-based systems anywhere, or is 'detection' purely a coincidental shared word?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Don't treat a shared link on this page as corroboration across sources -- these items are grouped by word overlap only; verify each independently before citing them together.

day_captions.c1f5f7897cab6194: General-purpose anomaly detection for relational databases -- no mention of language models; grouped here only by the shared word 'detection.'
day_captions.c6589f453fe3efd2: Anomaly detection robustness for industrial control systems under training-time data poisoning -- another 'detection' match with no LLM content.
day_captions.c8fa2c59f3b3c019: State-space streaming video anomaly detection -- a third unrelated 'detection' paper, not about language models.
day_captions.473e4a8407d950ff: Three named commercial assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek) compared head-to-head on one clinical patient-education task.
day_captions.44fdd531ea49fe98: Hallucination scoring read off internal activations at generation time, no output sampling required.
day_captions.7ac516e280c5ca22: A benchmark targeting dynamically orchestrated agent swarms rather than fixed-role multi-agent setups.
day_captions.c0d8647786942e91: A second hallucination-detection paper, this one for medical chatbot outputs, using multi-perspective adjudication instead of majority vote.
day_captions.5fc5b2481c7ef922: A domain-specific applications review: LLM readiness for building-energy HVAC automation.
day_captions.51d5a65d305149bc: Comparing two Chinese labs' commercial strategies -- unrelated to the other items in this title-phrase cluster.
day_captions.70ffdcd5e3598c72: The newest item: a domain-specific hallucination detector combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification with Monte Carlo sampling.
